summary: Step 6 fuses the three routes admitted to rank (phenotype from step 1, likelihood from step 4, knowledge from step 5) plus one confirmation-only route (read-derived evidence from steps 2-3, admitted at weight 0 because it measured zero discrimination between targets and decoys), using reciprocal rank fusion over 274 pairs drawn from a 51,410-pair universe. The fused ranking was frozen and sha256-hashed (`a596abf8…`) before any iteration-1 table was read — the blind gate stayed green through freezing and only flipped at the unblinding entry. The fused rank-1 pair is BUB1B, the same truncating (dbSNP rs759242053) + missense pair iteration 1 uploaded and had confirmed by the oracle. It holds rank 1 under both equal weights and measured-error-rate weights, and is corroborated by 3 of 4 disjoint evidence sources (clinical terms, VCF, raw reads — literature is missing). But a leave-one-route-out ablation shows the fusion is not four independent witnesses agreeing: silencing the likelihood route alone drops the leader from rank 1 to rank 62, while silencing either other route leaves it at rank 1. Of four pre-registered claims, two were refuted and two supported; a fifth entry then built and rehearsed — but did not upload — a second oracle submission to confirm it would teach nothing (0.000 bits expected information gain).
why: Every earlier step's route was validated in isolation, but none of them alone was allowed to be the final word: reciprocal rank fusion treats separate ranked lists as independent witnesses, and that assumption fails if the lists secretly share an input (two routes reading the same 8 clinical terms, two reading the same callset, one route seeded with another's output) — in which case a fused rank 1 could look like convergence while actually being one signal echoed. Without the leave-one-route-out ablation and the independent-evidence count, the report could not honestly distinguish 'four instruments converged on this answer' from 'one instrument found it and the others didn't disagree.' And without freezing the ranking's digest before reading any iteration-1 table, a rediscovery claim would be unfalsifiable — nothing would stop the comparison from being run, disliked, and quietly re-run until it matched.
verdict: H041 (fused rank 1 for the confirmed pair, and no admitted route ranks it below 3) is refuted on its second clause: fused rank 1 holds, but the phenotype route ranks it 9th of its own list and the knowledge route does not list it in its top 50 at all — only the likelihood route (rank 1) meets the bar. H042 (no single route carries the fused result) is refuted: removing the likelihood route drops the leader from rank 1 to rank 62, while removing phenotype or knowledge leaves it at rank 1 — the fusion is carried by one discriminating route, corroborated at a distance by the others, not four independent witnesses. H043 (the leader has ≥2 disjoint evidence inputs behind it) is supported: it has 3 of 4 (HPO, VCF, reads; literature is the one missing). H044 (a second oracle upload is not informative) is supported: expected information gain is 0.000 bits on all three testable questions (the causal pair, a second causal pair, and secondary findings), and a later entry (124) built and rehearsed the actual reserve submission file to confirm this on real bytes without uploading it — 5 of 6 oracle slots remain, deliberately.

inherits.what: Step 6 is the only step that reads all five predecessors' measured outputs directly rather than re-deriving anything: step 1's recall@300 (0.335) sets the phenotype route's measured weight and its admission as an enrichment; step 2's zero-discrimination finding (10/396 targets vs 10/396 decoys) is why the read route is admitted at weight 0 as confirmation-only, never as a ranking vote; step 3's dosage and copy-number findings become the per-gene confirmation triple (read-confirmed, single-copy, no CN loss); step 4's AUC 0.706 and permutation p=0.056 set the likelihood route's admission and its dominant measured weight (0.9441); step 5's AUC 0.634 sets the knowledge route's admission and weight, and its own admission rule (`RouteWeight.ranking_route`) is called rather than re-implemented.

hands_to.what: Step 7's Track 2 drug-repurposing enrichment inherits the confirmed, fused-rank-1 pair as the gene to build mechanism and drug-target evidence around — it can proceed on a gene the fusion corroborated from independent inputs, without needing to re-litigate whether the diagnosis holds. Step 6 also hands forward the disclosed weakness (one route carries the result) as a caveat Track 2's evidence chain should not overstate.

figures.name: agreement-matrix.png
figures.reads: A gene/pair-by-route grid: rows are the leading fused pairs (best fused rank first), columns are the four routes, each cell coloured by the rank that route gave the pair (green = rank 1, yellow shades = inside top 50, darker better, grey = never listed), asterisked cells marking a rank inherited from the pair's whole gene.
figures.means: The step's headline visual: BUB1B's row shows green (likelihood rank 1), a mid-yellow phenotype cell (rank 9), and a grey knowledge cell (never listed) — visually showing that 'agreement' here means one strong vote and two weak or absent ones, not four green cells.

figures.name: agreement-matrix.html
figures.reads: Interactive version of the same route-by-pair grid, with hover tooltips giving the exact rank per cell.
figures.means: Same evidence as the static grid, letting a reader check any cell's exact rank rather than reading it off a colour band.

figures.name: leave-one-route-out.png
figures.reads: Horizontal bars, one per route removed from the fusion, showing where the all-routes leader (BUB1B) lands with that route silenced; green bar = still rank 1, red bar = moved off rank 1, bar length is the new rank.
figures.means: Direct evidence for H042's refutation: removing `likelihood` sends the bar out to rank 62 (red), while removing `phenotype` or `knowledge` keeps it at rank 1 (green) — proof that one route, not a consensus of four, is carrying the fused result.

figures.name: leave-one-route-out.html
figures.reads: Interactive version of the leave-one-route-out bars, with hover tooltips for the exact rank each ablation produces.
figures.means: Same evidence as the static bars, letting a reader inspect exact post-ablation ranks.

figures.name: independent-evidence.png
figures.reads: Stacked bars per leading pair, one coloured segment per disjoint raw evidence source (purple = the 8 clinical terms, blue = the delivered callset/VCF, green = raw reads, yellow = published literature) that speaks for it, after collapsing routes that read the same source.
figures.means: Evidence for H043: BUB1B's stack has 3 segments (HPO, VCF, reads) and is missing the literature segment — a short stack overall would mean a pair nominated only by instruments reading the same underlying data; this correction is what prevents reciprocal rank fusion's blind spot (treating correlated lists as independent) from overstating how well-supported a pair is.

figures.name: independent-evidence.html
figures.reads: Interactive version of the stacked independent-evidence bars, with hover tooltips naming each segment's source.
figures.means: Same evidence as the static stacked bars, letting a reader confirm exactly which raw sources back each leading pair.

figures.name: weight-sensitivity.png
figures.reads: Paired bars per top gene: blue = rank under the pre-registered equal weighting, yellow = rank under each route's own measured error-rate weighting (symptom recall 0.335, 1−permutation-p 0.944, knowledge AUC 0.634); shorter bar is a better (lower) rank.
figures.means: The robustness check reported alongside, never instead of, the primary result: BUB1B stays at rank 1 under both weightings, which is the one robustness statement this step can make — while CLCNKB falls from rank 2 to 49 once weights reflect measured route quality, showing how sensitive the rest of the ranking is to the weighting choice.

figures.name: weight-sensitivity.html
figures.reads: Interactive version of the equal-weight vs measured-weight comparison, with hover tooltips for exact ranks under each weighting.
figures.means: Same evidence as the static bars, letting a reader inspect exact rank shifts gene by gene.

figures.name: decoy-reach.png
figures.reads: Bars showing the best fused rank reached by each gene class (targets vs. matched decoys), with diamonds marking the median fused rank per class; lower is better.
figures.means: The fusion's own decoy null: a matched control gene reaches fused rank 13, well inside the top 20, while targets have a median rank of 109 versus decoys' median of 42 — evidence that the fused ranking's resolution below rank 1 is poor, and that no claim should be made about ranks 2–20 as a clean candidate list.

figures.name: decoy-reach.html
figures.reads: Interactive version of the decoy-reach bars, with hover tooltips for exact best-rank and median-rank values per class.
figures.means: Same evidence as the static bars, letting a reader inspect the exact reach of the decoy null.

figures.name: freeze-receipt.html
figures.reads: A plain fact table (not a chart): the frozen file's path, its sha256 digest (`a596abf8…`), the row count (274), the freeze timestamp, and the fusion's fixed constants (k=60, top 50 per route, absent=rank 51, seed 20260918).
figures.means: The commitment device that makes the rediscovery claim falsifiable: this digest was written into methodology entry 108 before any iteration-1 table was read, so a re-run that disagreed with the answer could not silently replace it without producing a different, detectably mismatched hash.

figures.name: index.html
figures.reads: Interactive contact sheet combining all five chart exhibits (agreement-matrix, leave-one-route-out, independent-evidence, weight-sensitivity, decoy-reach) plus the freeze-receipt fact table.
figures.means: Same evidence as the individual exhibits, gathered on one page for the step's report view.
